﴿Al-Kitab al-Hakim﴾ (the Wise Book). Mentioned in Yunus.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31 (Luqman), verse 6:

﴿And among the people is one who purchases idle talk﴾ refers to singing (ghinā'). In a hadith, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Buying singing girls and selling them is forbidden (ḥarām)," and he recited this verse. It has also been said that it was revealed concerning a man of Quraysh who bought a singing slave-girl who would sing satires (hijā') of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). According to this view, "purchase" is meant literally (ḥaqīqa). It has also been said that it was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Ḥārith, who had learned the tales of the Persians (akhbār Fāris); this is what is meant by "idle talk," and "purchasing idle talk" means preferring it and listening to it. According to this view, "purchase" is used figuratively (majāz). It has also been said that "idle talk" means the drum (ṭabl), and it has been said that it means shirk. The wording of the phrase encompasses all of these. The apparent meaning of the verse is that it is idle talk that is directed toward disbelief in the religion and mockery, based on the words of the Exalted: ﴿that he may mislead from the way of Allah﴾ and the rest of the verse. It also indicates that the intended reference is a specific individual, since the verse goes on to describe him with a number of attributes.
﴿Without pillars that you can see﴾. Mentioned in al-Ra'd [2]. ﴿Lest it sway with you﴾, that is, lest it sway with you.

Luqman (لُقْمَانَ): a man who speaks with wisdom (الحكمة). Scholars differed over whether he was a prophet (نبيّ) or not. A hadith states: "Luqman was not a prophet, but he was a servant (عبداً) of good certainty (حسن اليقين), who loved Allah, so Allah loved him and bestowed wisdom upon him." It is narrated that he was the son of the sister of Ayyub (Job), or his maternal nephew. It is also narrated that he was the judge (قاضي) of the Children of Israel (بني إسرائيل). Scholars differed about his profession (صناعته): it is said he was a carpenter (نجاراً), and it is said a tailor (خياطاً), and it is said a shepherd of sheep (راعي غنم). His son was a disbeliever (كافراً), and he continued to advise him until he embraced Islam. It is narrated that the name of his son was Tharan (ثاران).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 14:

﴿And We have enjoined upon man﴾ This verse and the one following it are a parenthetical interjection within the admonition of Luqman to his son, for the sake of emphasis, because of what Luqman's admonition contains regarding the prohibition of associating partners with Allah. The verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother, as we mentioned in (surah) al-'Ankabut. ﴿His mother bore him in weakness upon weakness⦆ meaning, weakness upon weakness, because as the pregnancy grows heavier, the pregnant woman's weakness increases. ﴿Weakness upon weakness﴾ (wahnan) is in the accusative by an implied verb whose estimate is: she grows weak in weakness. ﴿And his weaning﴾ meaning his being weaned, and by this he indicated the maximum period of breastfeeding. ﴿That give thanks﴾ is an explanation of the admonition, and an interjection was placed between it and its explanation by His saying: ﴿And his weaning is in two years﴾, to show what the mother endures with the child, which necessitates her great right; and for this reason her right is greater than the father's right.

"O my son" (﴿يٰبُنَيَّ﴾), etc.: he has returned to the words of Luqman; the implied sense is: "And Luqman said: O my son."

﴿Indeed, if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed⁠

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 17:

﴿And be patient over what befalls you.﴾ This is a command to be patient over calamities in general. It has also been said that the meaning is what befalls one who enjoins good and forbids evil. ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ It may mean: of what Allah has commanded in the manner of resolve and obligation; or of the noble character traits that people of firm resolve and earnestness are determined to uphold. The word ʿazm (resolve) is a verbal noun used in the sense of the passive participle, meaning: of the matters that are resolved upon.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 18:

﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾. Al-ṣaʿr (الصعر) linguistically means inclination, so the meaning is: do not turn your cheek away from people and turn away from them out of arrogance toward them. ﴿Exultant﴾ (مرحاً) is mentioned in al-Isra' [37]. ﴿Boastful﴾ (مختال) comes from al-khuyala' (الخيلاء).

And moderate your pace in your walking (﴿وَٱقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ﴾): that is, keep to a balanced gait, neither hurrying in a way that shows frivolity and lightness, nor dragging your feet in a way that shows vanity and arrogance.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 20:

﴿His favours, outward and inward.﴾ The outward (ẓāhirah) are health, wealth and other such things; the inward (bāṭinah) are the favours that people do not perceive, among them the concealing of ugly deeds. It is also said: the outward are the favours of this world, and the inward are the favours of the Hereafter. The wording is more general than all of that.

﴿And among people is one who argues⁠﴾ It was revealed concerning al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and those like him.
﴿Even if Satan was calling them to the punishment of the Blazing Fire?﴾ Its meaning: will they follow their forefathers even if Satan is calling them to the Fire?

﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah﴾: "yuslim" means he sincerely devotes himself, or surrenders, or submits. "The face" here is an expression for intention. ﴿with the firmest handhold﴾: this was mentioned in al-Baqarah.
﴿Say: Praise be to God﴾ and what follows is mentioned in Surah al-ʿAnkabut.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 27:

﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea [were ink], replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted.﴾ This is an informing of the abundance of the words of Allah, and what is meant is the vastness of His knowledge. The meaning of the verse: if the trees of the earth were pens, and the sea were ink, with seven seas poured into it continuously, and the words of Allah were written with that, the trees and the seas would be exhausted, and the words of Allah would not be exhausted, because trees and seas are finite, while the words of Allah are infinite.

If it is said: Why did He not say "and the sea [were] ink" as He said in al-Kahf, "Say: If the sea were ink (midad) for the words of my Lord..."? The answer: His saying "yamudduhu" (replenishes it) suffices in place of that, since it derives from your saying madda al-dawah and amadda-ha (he supplied the inkwell).

If it is said: Why did He say "min shajarah" (from a tree) and not "min shajar" (from trees) in the collective noun form, which implies generality? The answer: He intended to detail the trees one by one, tree by tree, so that not a single one of them is left out.

If it is said: Why did He say "kalimat Allah" and not "kalim Allah" in the plural of abundance (jam' al-kathrah)? The answer: this is more eloquent, because if the words are not exhausted despite being in the plural of paucity (jam' qillah), then how could the plural of abundance be exhausted?

It is related that the occasion of the revelation of this verse was that the Jews said: "We have been given the Torah, and in it is all knowledge," so the verse was revealed to show that what they possess is little compared to the much. According to this view the verse is Medinan. It is also said that its occasion was that the Quraysh said: "The Qur'an will be exhausted."

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 28:

﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but like that of a single soul.﴾ This is an explanation of God's power to resurrect people, and a refutation of those who regard that as unlikely.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 29:

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾ meaning: He makes each of them enter into the other, so that one increases while the other decreases; or by the entering of the darkness of the night upon the light of the day, and the entering of the light of the day upon the darkness of the night. ﴿Until a specified term﴾ meaning: the Day of Resurrection.
﴿That is because Allah﴾. The bāʾ (ب) may be causal (sababiyyah), or the meaning may be: "That is because Allah is the Truth (al-ḥaqq), and that [He is] the One who is witnessing (shāhid)."

﴿بِنِعْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ It may be that by this he means what the ships carry of food and merchandise, and the باء (bāʾ) is for attachment (ilṣāq) or accompaniment (muṣāḥaba). Or he means the wind, in which case the باء is causal (sababiyya). ﴿صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾ is an intensive form (mubālaga, emphatic form) of صابر (ṣābir) and شاكر (shākir).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 31, verse 32:

﴿Like canopies﴾ The plural of ẓullah, which is that which overshadows you from above. The waves are likened to this when they rise and grow large until they tower over a person. ﴿Among them is one who is moderate﴾ The muqtaṣid (moderate one) is the one who is intermediate in the matter. It may mean a disbeliever who is moderate in his disbelief, not going to excess in it, or a believer who is moderate in his faith, because the sincerity (ikhlāṣ) he had at sea would leave him. It has also been said: the meaning of muqtaṣid is a believer who remained steadfast on land to what he pledged to God at sea. ﴿Treacherous⦆ That is, betrayer, extremely treacherous. This is because he denied God's blessing through betrayal.

"No father will avail anything for his son, nor will a son avail anything for his father"—that is, he will not discharge anything on his behalf. The meaning is that it will not benefit him, nor avert any harm from him. "Nor will a child (mawlud)"—that is, a son—so just as a father cannot do anything for his son, likewise a son cannot do anything for his father. "The Deceiver" (al-Gharur) is Satan; it has also been said that it refers to false hope and procrastination.

﴿The knowledge of the Hour﴾: that is, when it will occur. This is among the things that God alone has knowledge of. For this reason it is reported in the hadith: "The keys of the unseen are five." He then recited this verse: ﴿What will he earn tomorrow?﴾, meaning good or evil, wealth or children, or other than that.
